items.title: Oliver Nelson Jr. interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, September 10, 2020
items.q: if I could go out and play post-bop like Joe Henderson and those guys, that’s the music that I really love.

ctx.x: Do you have your own, I mean you pretty much just said it, do you have your own opinion on the jazz education as a whole in the United States? It’s certainly a big business and there’s a built-in issue with all these graduates, what are they going to do in a business that isn’t as robust as the education.

I think you said it best when you said when we were talking before, you said, this: you’ve got to be versatile. See the days for me, if I could go out and play post-bop like Joe Henderson and those guys, that’s the music that I really love. You’re not going to eat on that. You’ve got to find a way to eat, man. So if Kanye’s got something and he needs a saxophone player to come in to play something, you’ve got to be able to play with him. Or if the symphony is doing a Ravel piece and they need a saxophone player…
